notes: PARTIAL (2026-11-16, the 1985 code reads, cause b: wrong the same way at every edition): the mechanism of kb/Work PB5810: PB5810 - RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON a table element is accepted and the length is then ignored at run time (every edition). Owner: kb/Work PB5810 (open). Ruled in kb/Work/PB5683/2026-11-15-rulings-code-reads-batch-7.md; the 1985 rows that carry into this rule: 1985-GR-VIII.3.2.4-5, 1985-GR-XI.3.2.4-2. Recorded by the registrar from the ruling and its note, the repro not re-run by the registrar. The prose that follows is the stored CONFORMS account, kept as the account of the part that holds. || The format is `SD file-name-1 [ record-clause ] .` and nothing else, RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p376 / printed folio 346) rather than read off the OCR. Both halves hold: the record-clause is modelled and the file-name-only spelling parses (the positive golden writes `SD SF RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS.`), and the residue is now DIAGNOSED. The rule used to end in a generic file-description clause (`IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER|literal)*`), a shared vendor-extension catch-all that made `SD SF WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compile and run in silence at every edition (kb/Work PB829); it now ends in the ONE `unrecognizedClause` error production, refused by name with COBOL1970. The COBOL-85 DATA RECORDS clause of this format is superset-parsed and removal-gated post-bind. A green witness that the legal clause parses would NOT have been evidence on its own — the row also owes the negative, because an open list can parse every legal clause and still accept anything at all.
